title: Test Activities and Tasks
concept:
The test process is the set of activities performed to plan, design, execute, and report on testing. ISTQB groups test activities into a logical, iterative sequence that recurs at every test level (component, integration, system, acceptance):

**Test Planning** — defining test objectives, approach, schedule, scope, and resources. The test plan is updated as the project evolves.

**Test Monitoring and Control** — collecting metrics on test progress and product quality, comparing them to the plan, and taking corrective action.

**Test Analysis** — analysing the test basis (requirements, designs, code) to identify what to test and to derive test conditions, including risk assessment.

**Test Design** — elaborating test conditions into concrete test cases with inputs, expected results, and execution preconditions.

**Test Implementation** — creating or organising what's needed to run tests: test data, environments, automation scripts, test suites.

**Test Execution** — running the tests (manually or automatically), comparing actual to expected results, and logging incidents.

**Test Completion** — closing the test activity: archiving artifacts, evaluating lessons learned, communicating results to stakeholders.

The activities are not strictly sequential — analysis, design, and implementation often run in parallel, and monitoring/control runs throughout.
keyPoints: Seven test activities: planning, monitoring & control, analysis, design, implementation, execution, completion.
Activities are iterative and overlapping, not strictly sequential.
Monitoring and control runs throughout to keep testing aligned with the plan and adjust when conditions change.

quiz.question: Which test activity is concerned with creating concrete test cases (inputs, expected results, preconditions) from previously identified test conditions?
quiz.explanation: Test design transforms abstract test conditions (identified during test analysis) into concrete test cases. Test implementation then prepares the data, environment, and scripts needed to actually run those cases.
